summary.text: 语 is the standardized simplified form of 語, meaning “language” or “words” and associated with speaking. In 語, 言 supplies the speech-related meaning and 吾 serves as a sound element; the simplified form writes 言 as 讠. [ref003, ref004, ref008, ref020]

formation.text: The traditional graph 語 is phonosemantic: 言 contributes the speech-related meaning, while 吾 supplies a sound cue. The simplified graph 语 writes 言 as 讠 in left-side position. A graphic-history account reports early bronze forms with differing phonetic shapes, including one resembling a complex 五; that shape’s identity and pronunciation are unresolved. [ref008, ref018, ref020, ref022, ref023, ref027]

components.text: 讠 is the standardized simplified left-side form of 言 in 语. It contributes the speech-related meaning that 言 bears in traditional 語; it does not independently supply a sound cue here. [ref008, ref020]

吾 is identified as the phonetic element in traditional 語. Early bronze forms are also reported with another phonetic shape resembling a complex 五, but its identity and relationship to 吾 are unresolved. [ref008, ref018, ref022, ref027]

sound.text: These system-specific reconstructions are similar enough to support a proposed historical sound relationship; they are reconstructed forms, not recorded ancient pronunciations. [ref009, ref021, ref022]
The reconstructed Middle Chinese readings preserve a comparison, although the forms differ. [ref021, ref022]
The modern Mandarin readings differ and do not by themselves demonstrate the historical relationship. [ref005, ref012, ref022]

history.text: The received traditional analysis writes 語 with 言 and 吾. A graphic-history account reports bronze examples with two phonetic shapes, one resembling a complex 五 and another identified as 吾; from Warring States script onward, it analyzes the form as 言 plus 吾. The curated seal-style drawings show 言 and 吾 separately in modern redrawings, not 語 or its early inscription forms. [ref008, ref018, ref027, ref028, ref029]
In standardized simplified 语, the 言 radical is written 讠 in left-side position. [ref003, ref020]

uncertainties.text: The reported early bronze phonetic shape resembling a complex 五 has no established original identity or pronunciation here. The later 吾 analysis and sound comparison do not settle those questions. [ref018, ref022, ref027]
A proposal derives 言 from 語 with a nominal suffix, but the supporting discussion was not independently inspected; the proposal remains secondary and unconfirmed here. [ref009, ref023]

senses.period: dating unresolved; cited in an Analects example
senses.text: One cited Analects passage uses 語 for speaking or discussing. The surviving witness is not dated here, so this example does not establish the earliest attested use. [ref017, ref026]

senses.period: dating unresolved; cited in an Analects example
senses.text: A separate cited Analects passage uses 語 for telling or addressing. Its chronological relation to the speak/discuss use is unresolved. [ref017, ref026]

Current dictionary meanings include language, words, saying, and expression. The evidence does not establish when these uses developed in relation to the cited speak/discuss and tell uses. [ref004, ref011, ref026]

limitations.text: Other recorded senses include literary wording, signals, and animal calls, but the evidence gives no dated sequence linking them to the speak/discuss, tell, or current meanings. [ref026]
The surviving witnesses behind the cited historical examples are not dated, and no chronology connecting those uses to current meanings is established. [ref017, ref026]

overview.text: 语 means “language” or “words” and is linked with speaking. It is simplified from 語: 言 is written 讠, while 吾 is the sound element in the traditional graph. [ref003, ref004, ref008, ref020]

components.text: 讠 is the simplified left-side form of 言, which contributes the speech-related meaning in 語. [ref008, ref020]
吾 is the sound element in traditional 語. Its older reconstructed reading is similar to 語’s, though the modern Mandarin readings differ. [ref008, ref021, ref022]

relationships.text: In simplified 语, 讠 is the standardized left-side form of 言 and carries its speech-related contribution; the traditional graph 語 is analyzed with 言 in this position. [ref008, ref020]

The received analysis identifies 吾 as the sound element in 語. Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese reconstructions for 吾 (*ŋˤa) and 語 (*ŋ(r)aʔ) are similar enough to support a historical phonetic relation, despite differing notation and modern Mandarin readings. A separate early bronze shape resembling a complex 五 is reported, but its identity and relation to 吾 remain unresolved. [ref008, ref018, ref021, ref022, ref027]
语 is the standardized simplified counterpart of 語; the 言 radical is written 讠 in left-side position under the simplification rule. [ref003, ref020]
